headToHead.voiceVerdict: Bar. Cover the names and Polly is identified by sentence shape: she asks a question and answers it herself ('Are you with me? Obviously you're with me.'), chains with 'So,' 'Anyway,' 'huh?', and misreads mortal stakes as gossip. Pixel is identified by nouns (clip, stream, mod, autoplay, chat), not by shape. Strip the streamer words and 'Stop thanking me for my patience. I have none.' is Maximilian, 'Same time tomorrow. Bring better bots.' is any host, and 'Brock, loudest bot... Only bot...' is Vera's repeat-then-turn. Pixel's one true shape, the mid-sentence drop, appears six times and only in the unsure slot, four of six times via 'sorry', which is Tilly's tic.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Bar, narrowly. Ours wins on economy (Polly runs 25 words; our best is 7). But four of our twelve best get their laugh from the rival's premise said back (fee, thee, patience, autoplay): the turn is borrowed, not built from Pixel's own logic. Polly builds her turns from her own want: literalism pushed upward ('fun' in 'funeral', electric slide with actual electricity, 'what kills people'). Pixel's engine is deflation (score, skip), which is one move repeated; Polly's is escalation, which keeps producing new images. 'Six, minus the processing fee. So, four.' is the only line in the bank that does both: rival's premise plus Pixel's own score logic in a real turn.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar. 'Put the fun back in funeral', 'hard to keep track of what kills people', 'hay bbe lez party' get clipped. Ours: 'Massive moth' and 'Ending stream before I get bored of ending stream' would get clipped; the rest are competent beats nobody repeats tomorrow.

notes: Bar file existed and was read in full (Polly lines verbatim from it; two of the bar's twelve are player options written for Polly's events, flagged as such). The bar is not flawless: 'ghostsip as I like to call it' explains its own joke and two Polly lines run past our 20-word limit. Our bank is clean on mechanical rules; its problem is sameness. Counted 191 lines (ex lines included); 112 are generic or templated (58.6%). Pixel has no X-but-secretly-Y in the lines: Polly is a party ghost who misreads death, Pixel is a bored streamer who is bored. The ex lines ('leaves at ninety-nine percent', 'opened another tab') hint at the real contradiction, a judge who never finishes anything either, and that is never turned on Pixel by Pixel. Pixel also never wants anything in a line. Monster Prom lines end by demanding something; Pixel's questions do ('If it's a mug, I end stream.') but the reactions only rate. Protect the moth line but kill the other five drops; one drop per episode is a bit, six is a template. 'Chat's typing thee now. You started a whole thing.' is the model for what chat should do everywhere: chat reacts specifically and the reaction is the joke.
